in_arabic.name: سُحُف
in_arabic.long_meaning: سُحُفُ في اللغة العربية تعني الكتب أو الأوراق القديمة، ويُنسب هذا الاسم إلى سُحُف إبراهيم عليه السلام، والتي ذكرها القرآن الكريم كسُحُفِ حُكيَمةٍ، أي سُحُفٌ مُكَتوبةٌ بِالحكمة، وتُشير إلى كِتَاباتٍ مُعَقّدةٍ وذات أُصولٍ قديمةٍ.  ومنذ ذلك الحين، يُستَعمل اسم سُحُف لِيمُرّرُ إلى الأوراق والكتب القديمة،  وخاصةً تلكِ التي تُحَفظُ بِحُفَظةٍ وُقَدُرَةٍ.

in_urdu.name: سُحُف
in_urdu.meaning: قدیم کتابوں اور صفحات کا نام
in_urdu.long_meaning: سُحُف ایک عربی لفظ ہے جس کا مطلب قدیم کتابوں یا صفحات سے ہوتا ہے۔ یہ نام حضرت ابراہیم علیہ السلام کی سُحُف سے ماخوذ ہے، جن کا ذکر قرآن مجید میں حُکمایة کی سُحُف کے طور پر کیا گیا ہے۔ یہ سُحُف حکمت سے بھری ہوئی کتابیں تھیں۔ اس نام کی وجہ سے سُحُف کا استعمال قدیم اور قیمتی کتابوں اور صفحات کے لیے کیا جاتا ہے۔

in_hindi.name: सुहुफ
in_hindi.meaning: प्राचीन ग्रंथों या पन्नों का नाम
in_hindi.long_meaning: सुहुफ एक अरबी शब्द है जिसका अर्थ पुराने ग्रंथों या पन्नों को दर्शाता है। इसका उद्गम खलीफा अबू बकर सिद्धीकी के पुस्तकालय से है। इस शब्द का उपयोग अरब संस्कृति में पुराने और महत्वपूर्ण ग्रंथों के लिए किया जाता है।

in_pashto.name: سوحو
in_pashto.meaning: پښتو کې د قدیم کتابو او ورغو نوم
in_pashto.long_meaning: سوحو په پښتو کې د قدیم کتابو او ورغو نوم دی.  د قرآن کریم په کتاب کې د ابراهام (ع) د سوحو ترڅو باندې خبر وړلای شوی دی چې د حکمت او دانش د کتابو په توګه وروسته هم د سوحو په نوم یادونه کېږي.

data.cultural_impact: The name Suhuf holds a significant cultural impact in Islamic history as it is associated with the Suhuf or the tablets that Allah (swt) had given to Prophet Moses (as). This event is mentioned in various chapters of the Quran including Al-Anbiya (21:5-7), Al-A'raf (7:145), and Al-Shuaraa'(26:2-8). This tale carries numerous lessons and emphasizes the sovereignty of Allah, Prophet Moses' unwavering faith, and Allah's promise to protect and preserve His revelations.
data.spiritual_significance: The spiritual significance of the name Suhuf lies in the belief that it is a reminder of the divine messages and tablets, Allah's preservation and protection of sacred knowledge, and His role as the communication link between Himself and His Prophets and creation. Suhuf, as a name, evokes feelings of respect, reverence, and awe toward the divine, emphasizing the importance of preserving and upholding sacred knowledge and values. Additionally, it could be viewed as a reminder of the importance of hifz (memorization) and protection of the Quran as the sacred text, reinforcing the spiritual bond between the Muslim and their faith and practice.

historical_references.reference: Ibn Abd al-Hakam, Futuh Misr (conquests of Egypt), 12th century CE. Suhuf mentioned as a type of papyrus scroll used for writing the Quran and other religious texts.
historical_references.context: Religious texts written on suhuf scrolls

historical_references.reference: Al-Masudi, Muruj al-Dhahab (Meadows of Gold), 10th century CE. Suhuf mentioned as a type of preserved tablets used by Prophet Musa (Moses) and Prophet Harun (Aaron) to communicate God's messages to Pharaoh.

modern_usage.modern_context: The term 'Suhuf' refers to the sacred scripts and texts written by Prophet Muhammad (PBUH) himself or his companions. In modern times, the significance of Suhuf has been revived and celebrated in various ways. On social media platforms like Instagram and Pinterest, users create and share content showcasing the beauty and intricacy of Islamic calligraphy, which is often inspired by the Suhuf. Additionally, digital preservation and archiving initiatives have taken an interest in this historical practice, making digitized copies of ancient Suhuf available to scholars and the public. The Google Arts & Culture platform, for instance, features a section dedicated to exploring the history and significance of Suhuf through various exhibitions and resources.
